keys.statement: Split an alcohol-water heterogeneous azeotrope with a decanter and two strippers: the organic layer gives dry alcohol at the bottom of one, the aqueous layer gives water at the bottom of the other, and both overheads return to the decanter.

decisions.mechanism: The azeotrope splits into two liquids that lie on either side of it.
limits: Shown for isobutanol; 1-butanol + water forms the same kind of azeotrope, a transfer not tested here.

keys.statement: Adding a strong salting-out salt (potassium carbonate) raised the alcohol's partition and dehydration with the salt staying in the aqueous phase, and salting-out plus distillation used less energy than solvent extraction.

decisions.mechanism: Ions bind water and push the alcohol out.
